title: Capacity phased adoption logistics — NA/EU/APAC (Q3–Q4 2026)
body:
Summary:
This is a tactical playbook for rolling additional GPU capacity into our NA / EU / APAC fleets across multiple cloud vendors during Q3–Q4 2026. The goal is to provision a predictable runway that matches forecasted customer demand while maintaining our 70% long-run utilization target and a 15–25% operational buffer for surge. This doc captures staging windows, activation criteria, monitoring queries, rollback triggers, and handoffs to SRE/Capacity Ops.

Context & objectives:
- We expect token-based demand to grow ~42% across hosted workloads from Jul–Dec 2026 driven by new PLG signups and a mid-market customer cohort.
- Target long-run utilization per region fleet: 60–75% (with different optimal points by instance class).
- Maintain immediate surge headroom: min 15% spare capacity in NA/EU, 20% in APAC due to less predictable demand patterns.
- Prefer phased onboards to avoid noisy neighbor issues and to validate kernel/runtime choices per model mix.

High-level rollout approach (phases):
1) Phase A — Validation lanes (small, regional): 2–3 small batches per region to validate provisioning scripts, network egress policies, and KV cache priming.
2) Phase B — Bulk activation (steady ramp): larger waves that bring fleets to 40–60% of target capacity per region.
3) Phase C — Full target + buffer: top-off to target GPU count and enable burst policies and autoscaler stretch windows.

Activation cadence (suggested):
- NA (primary US-West / US-East mix): Phase A start: 2026-07-05, Phase B start: 2026-07-19, Phase C finish: 2026-08-09
- EU (frankfurt, ireland mix): Phase A start: 2026-08-02, Phase B start: 2026-08-16, Phase C finish: 2026-09-06
- APAC (tokyo, sydney initially): Phase A start: 2026-09-01, Phase B start: 2026-09-21, Phase C finish: 2026-10-12

Region activation table (text spreadsheet):
Region | Cloud / Zone | Target GPUs (A100-80GB-equivalent) | Baseline util target | Buffer % | Activation window | Primary owner
NA     | GCP-us-west1 | 480 | 68% | 18% | 2026-07-05 -> 2026-08-09 | Ben Morales
NA     | AWS-us-east-1 | 360 | 70% | 15% | 2026-07-12 -> 2026-08-09 | Ben Morales
EU     | GCP-europe-west1 | 260 | 65% | 15% | 2026-08-02 -> 2026-09-06 | Liu Zhang
EU     | Azure-north-europe | 200 | 67% | 15% | 2026-08-09 -> 2026-09-06 | Liu Zhang
APAC   | GCP-asia-northeast1 | 140 | 60% | 20% | 2026-09-01 -> 2026-10-12 | Sofia Reyes
APAC   | AWS-ap-southeast-2 | 120 | 62% | 20% | 2026-09-08 -> 2026-10-12 | Sofia Reyes

Notes on instance mix and equivalency:
- All GPUs normalized to A100-80GB equivalent for planning. If vendor-delivered instance types differ, convert using our cost/perf table (see linked GH PR).
- For EU we will prefer a higher ratio of mid-memory instances to align with typical model sequence lengths there.

Pre-activation checklist (Phase A):
- Provisioning pipeline green for target instance types (PR #210 merged).
- KMS/HSM key material present and validated in region (security signoff).
- Network egress quotas requested and approved.
- Load-test job executed (ramp to 30% util for 2 hours) with KV cache warmup script.
- Telemetry: traces, token-level cost, per-route p50/p95 latency dashboards created and shared with SRE.
- Run blocker items: any open P0s on provisioning automation must be cleared.

Acceptance criteria (per-phase):
- Phase A: successful warm-up run, <1% rate-limited/io errors, p95 latency within expected band for baseline requests, no >10% QoS degradation reported by two sample customers.
- Phase B: sustained 48-hour run at incremental target util (40–60% of target) with autoscaler behaving as expected and cost drift <5% vs projection.
- Phase C: fleet can handle 110% of expected peak with buffer available, A/B traffic routed back to prod, documented rollback validated.

Monitoring & key queries (examples to paste into Grafana):
- Fleet utilization (per-region): sum(active_gpu_seconds) / (total_gpu_seconds) over 1h window -> alert if >82% for 30m
- Cold start rate: count(cold_start) / count(requests) -> alert if >0.8% sustained over 1h during Phase A/B
- Token cost delta: reported_cost / projected_cost -> alert if >1.12
- Error budget burn: derived from per-route 5xx and 429 rates, notify on >50% of daily budget in 4h

Rollback and mitigation triggers:
- Immediate rollback to previous capacity if p95 generation latency increases by >200ms and error rate >1% sustained for 15m.
- If noisy neighbor signs (one tenant causing >30% variance in host saturation), isolate via per-tenant throttles and pause activation queue for that zone.
- Contingency vendor switch: keep a hot spare fleet on alternate vendor in the region (10–15% of target) that can be promoted in 4–6h if provider outage occurs.

Cost & commit considerations:
- Mix of committed and on-demand capacity: aim for 60% committed in NA/EU for price predictability, 40% in APAC due to short-term uncertainty.
- Rough 6-month cost delta estimate for full target (all regions) = ~USD 2.1M (subject to final instance SKUs and discount tiers).

Operational handoffs (who does what):
- Provisioning: Ben / infra-provisioning
- Runtime validation & kernels: Serving Runtime team (PR #210 for kernel selection)
- Telemetry and dashboards: Observability (Liu) + SRE on-call for escalation
- Cost governance: Finance + Capacity Ops (monthly review)

Open questions / risks (notes to self):
- APAC demand shape still noisy — need one additional week of sandbox traffic analysis before Phase B.
- KMS access pattern: confirm we have regional KMS quotas and rotation automation for private deployments.
- If spot eviction rates climb (vendor-specific), how will autoscaler adjust? add a parameterized eviction-handling policy.

Follow-ups and next steps:
- Schedule a dry-run on 2026-06-30 for provisioning pipeline and runbook walkthrough (invite: infra, serving runtime, observability, security).
- Finalize the instance equivalency matrix and post to Confluence (owner: Ben, due 2026-02-20).
- Lock in committed capacity negotiations with primary vendors by 2026-03-15 to secure pricing.

Appendix (quick checklist for on-call during activation):
- Slack channel: #infra-capacity (bookmark)
- Pager rota: infra-oncall -> escalate to infra-leads after 20m
- Quick rollback command: infractl scale region <region> --to <previous-count> --immediate
- Runbook link: https://confluence.redwood/infra/runbooks/fleet-activation (draft)

End-of-doc — rough draft. This one should be used as the canonical staging playbook for regional rollouts unless changes are introduced in the planning sync.

Unresolved: list of dependent PRs and exact committed contract numbers (fill in after vendor negotiations).
